buyer_question: We are acquiring a news-monitoring pipeline built on newspaper3k — does the library still install and import cleanly on a current Python with current lxml, is its CI badge meaningful, and do the README's scraping examples still work?

claims.text: Installing the package with `pip3 install newspaper3k` on a current Python yields a working library: `import newspaper` and `from newspaper import Article` succeed.
claims.probe_hint: python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install newspaper3k && /tmp/v/bin/python -c 'from newspaper import Article; print("ok")'  # expect ImportError from lxml.html.clean with lxml>=5.2

claims.text: Newspaper (newspaper3k) is a Python 3 library; the python2 branch is deprecated and the python2 package on PyPI is named 'newspaper', not 'newspaper3k'.
claims.source_quote: **Newspaper is a Python3 library**! Or, view our **deprecated and buggy** `Python2 branch`_
claims.probe_hint: curl -s https://pypi.org/pypi/newspaper3k/json | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['info']['version'], [c for c in d['info']['classifiers'] if 'Python' in c])"

claims.text: The newspaper README displays a Travis CI build-status badge served from travis-ci.org, asserting a live, passing CI build for codelucas/newspaper.
claims.probe_hint: curl -sIL https://travis-ci.org/codelucas/newspaper.svg | head -5  # travis-ci.org was shut down in 2021; check what the badge actually serves

claims.text: With newspaper3k installed, downloading and parsing the URL http://fox13now.com/2013/12/30/new-year-new-laws-obamacare-pot-guns-and-drones/ via Article(url); article.download(); article.parse() yields article.authors == ['Leigh Ann Caldwell', 'John Honway'] and article.publish_date == datetime.datetime(2013, 12, 30, 0, 0).
claims.source_quote:
>>> article.parse()

    >>> article.authors
    ['Leigh Ann Caldwell', 'John Honway']

    >>> article.publish_date
    datetime.datetime(2013, 12, 30, 0, 0)
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from newspaper import Article; a=Article('http://fox13now.com/2013/12/30/new-year-new-laws-obamacare-pot-guns-and-drones/'); a.download(); a.parse(); print(a.authors, a.publish_date)"

claims.text: With newspaper3k installed and NLP corpora available, calling article.nlp() after download() and parse() populates article.keywords (a list of keyword strings) and article.summary (a summary string).
claims.source_quote:
>>> article.nlp()

    >>> article.keywords
    ['New Years', 'resolution', ...]

    >>> article.summary
    'The study shows that 93% of people ...'
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "from newspaper import Article; a=Article('<any live article url>'); a.download(); a.parse(); a.nlp(); assert a.keywords and a.summary"  # will raise if nltk punkt corpora not downloaded

claims.text: The NLP corpora required by newspaper3k can be installed by piping the repository script to python3: `curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/codelucas/newspaper/master/download_corpora.py | python3`.
On Debian/Ubuntu, the README's listed image-processing prerequisite `sudo apt-get install libjpeg-dev zlib1g-dev libpng12-dev` works as written (i.e. the package libpng12-dev is installable).
claims.source_quote:
- If you are on Python 3 install the distribution wide requirements::

    $ sudo apt-get install libjpeg-dev zlib1g-dev libpng12-dev
claims.probe_hint: docker run --rm ubuntu:24.04 bash -c 'apt-get update -qq && apt-cache show libpng12-dev' # package removed after Ubuntu 16.04; README itself notes a fallback

claims.text: With newspaper3k importable, `newspaper.languages()` prints the table of available input language codes (ar, be, bg, da, de, el, en, es, ...).
claims.source_quote:
>>> import newspaper
    >>> newspaper.languages()

    Your available languages are:
    input code      full name

claims.text: newspaper3k provides a multi-threaded article download framework importable as `from newspaper import news_pool`.
With newspaper3k installed, `newspaper.build('http://cnn.com')` returns a Source object whose .articles list contains Article objects with populated .url attributes.
claims.source_quote:
>>> cnn_paper = newspaper.build('http://cnn.com')

    >>> for article in cnn_paper.articles:
    >>>     print(article.url)
claims.probe_hint: python3 -c "import newspaper; p=newspaper.build('http://cnn.com', memoize_articles=False); print(len(p.articles), p.articles[0].url if p.articles else 'EMPTY')"

claims.text: The newspaper README claims the Swiftproxy residential-proxy service offers '80M+ residential IPs across 195+ countries' and 'a 99.89% success rate' for use with newspaper3k pipelines.
claims.source_quote: `Swiftproxy`_ — 80M+ residential IPs across 195+ countries, a 99.89% success rate, non-expiring traffic, and a free trial so you can pressure-test it before paying.
claims.probe_hint: No executable probe: vendor marketing claim embedded in the README; verify only that the claim is unsubstantiated third-party advertising (curl the vendor page and note absence of methodology)
